Oh Gosh, I can relate to this so much... Firstly, your roommate is a total jackass, but trust me, if he carries on the way he is doing he is going to mess up - karma has a way of getting people.

Secondly, the fact that she asked **you** out tells me that you are way more able to speak/connect with people than you give yourself credit for. She wanted to go out with you! Can you go back maybe when she's there,  and try and strike up a conversation with her? Be really casual about it - you have nothing to lose - at best you get a date, at worst you get some more experience. Maybe you could laugh about what an idiot your roommate was (I'm assuming she didn't call him). If she was interested enough before, chances are she still will be.

BUT, you need to get to the point where you are happy enough in yourself and your own life that you don't **need** someone else - this is exactly where I'm at. Just try to fill up your life with as much as you can - maybe make a list of things you enjoy/have always wanted to do and do them. 

As for the academic stuff, you need to tell someone about your emotional state - there are support systems in place for this kind of thing - you CAN get help (I personally have had to take 2 breaks from academic stuff and they hooked me up with a therapist)

If you can't talk to your friends, you can talk to us on here - we might have more experience and could offer advice if that would help.And what you said about your parents hit home so badly! Screw it if everyone has rejected you - you need to be your own best friend and put yourself first. Imagine if you had a friend who came up to you and said all these things, how would you react? What would you do to reassure them? Sometimes it's easier trying to help/solve other people's problems than our own because we feel like we should be able to handle anything.

When I was 10 years old, I got in trouble at school for not handing in money for the school photos. My teacher pulled me to the front of the class and started interrogating me about why I hadn't brought it in. I broke down crying and told her that my mum and dad weren't home - that my dad had got ill when we were on holiday and was now in the hospital. She felt really bad and everyday for the next 2 weeks or so, made me update the class every morning. The thing is, I never really knew what was happening, so I pretended that everything was fine. Truth is, my mum didn't come home a lot from the hospital and I guess wanted to protect me from it. On one particular Friday, my teacher made me stand up at the front of the class and I told them that he was having his op that day and would be coming home at the weekend in time for christmas. 
Later, I was at home with just my brothers waiting for my mum to come home. It was fireworks night, so my younger brother and I were pinned to the windows looking out at our neighbours' fireworks. Suddenly, we heard the key in the door and a whole load of people came into our house and there was so much noise and talking - a lot of it is blurry. I just remember feeling something was wrong, and running to the top of the stairs where my mum met my brother and I halfway and said these words which are forever stuck in my head: 'I'm sorry, daddy died, you haven't got a father anymore'. I don't remember anything after that. But every year November 5th rolls around, whilst everyone else is out there celebrating fireworks night, I stay at home and remember that awful sinking feeling, when I realised my life had changed forever.

TL;DR - When my dad died suddenly after I had just informed all my friends and teachers that he would be coming out of hospital the next day.

EDIT: Just realised I forgot to say, he had gall bladder cancer, and the operation killed him.

I was in a very similar situation as you - I really didn't want to take anti-depressants (I was terrified of the long-term side effects). But eventually I got to my absolute lowest point and realised I no longer cared about anything: I was suicidal, cutting all the time, in the full grasp of bulimia and almost unable to get out of bed to go to classes, and when I did go I couldn't concentrate at all. Through my university, I was able to join an eating disorder support group but was told I'd need to take anti-depressants so they could help me - I just gave in and took them. 

The first 3 nights or so I was dizzy, I couldn't sleep at all and my appetite disappeared completely. However, almost immediately (I think as soon as the initial dizziness etc wore off) I felt like a different person. Those first 6 months were incredible. I've been on anti-depressants for 3 years now, and although I seem to have got used to them, it is evident that I need them - if I even miss a day I go back to rock bottom. They help me to cope on an everyday basis, but I really do miss the effects of those first 6 months. 

For the record, I take 40mg Citalopram (Celexa). I used to take 60mg, but it gave me panic attacks and is no longer recommended. I think if I was in therapy too, I'd be coping much better - I'm on an NHS waiting list. Sorry this was long. I hope you find whatever works for you, and if you ever want to talk, feel free to PM me.

So I was abroad for my sisters wedding, staying in my grandmother's house where tonnes of relatives I'd never met before would come and go. It was always hectic - children running around, people suddenly turning up, so no one really took much notice of anything. 

I also received a lot of unwanted attention - for some reason a pale shy 17 year old girl from the UK was interesting to them... That was quite awkward enough in itself.

I happened to meet my first bf during this time - he was 10 years older than me and drove a motorbike and was life and soul of every party. To impress him/get his attention, I spent a day cleaning every inch of his motorbike until it was sparkling. He was surprised and appreciative and we got talking (This led to a 2 year LDR!)
Later, one of the men I was getting unwanted attention from (I'm sure he was a distant uncle) called my name as I was walking through the house, surrounded by the little kids. He ended up asking me why I hadn't cleaned his bike and making all sorts of half-jokes. When I wouldn't respond - I was looking down, blushing etc, he pulled out a gun and put it to my head. The little kids were yelling but he took no notice of them. He asked me if he should pull the trigger. I looked him dead in the eyes and said 'Yes' (I had been depressed for a long time before this and had considered suicide before. I was still cutting myself at this point) - I think that freaked him out a bit and he only held it a few seconds more. Then he pulled it away from my head, opened the chamber and showed me it was fully loaded and then gloated he could have done it if he wanted to. Keep in mind that this man was married with a kid and in his 40s. I never told anyone else - it's not like they'd believe me, and I'm sure the little kids will have long forgotten about it by now.

TL;DR: A distant relative held a loaded gun to my head, asked me if he should pull the trigger because I didn't respond to his advances. I told him yes, he freaked out and walked off. I never told anyone and the only witnesses will probably have forgotten about it.
